title: Sec sync — lab rotations & triage notes (Nov 15 2026)
content:
Attendees: Ethan Clarke (owner), Ava Martinez, Sofia Kim, Jonah Patel, Maya Singh, Noah Rivera
Date: 2026-11-15
Location: Zoom + huddle room B, ad-hoc lab environment

Purpose and context:
- Weekly security engineering sync focused on rotating the triage "lab" slot, validating recent secrets scans, and a short threat-modeling micro-workshop for the dedicated-capacity control plane.
- This doc is a working notes artifact for the week; capture of decisions, temporary mitigations, and concrete owners for follow-ups.

Agenda: (30m)
1) Quick triage queue review (10m)
2) Secrets scanning: false positives & escalation path (8m)
3) Threat modeling micro-workshop: Dedicated control plane (8m)
4) Action items & next rotation planning (4m)

1) Triage queue summary (owner: Ava)
- Open triage items: 9 total (reduced from 12 last week). Priority breakdown: P0:1, P1:3, P2:5.
- Notable tickets discussed:
  - JIRA-SEC-8421 (P0) — exposed internal metrics endpoint in staging that allowed unauthenticated read of shard utilization. Repro & scope: Jonah validated on staging-3; no customer data present. Root cause: missing ingress auth on a canary service after CI rollout.
    - Decision: Emergency ACL applied (no config drift expected) and orchestration runbook updated. Temporary mitigation implemented by infra: deny-all ingress -> then allow only via aggregator service.
    - Next steps: full incident RCA assigned to Jonah (ETA 2026-11-22). Postmortem template PR to be opened for exec summary.
  - JIRA-SEC-8430 (P1) — token leakage suspicion from third-party SDK in a vendor test harness. Evidence weaker: token appears truncated, likely a redaction/formatting issue.
    - Action: Maya to run a focused tracer on test harness and add a negative test case (deadline 2026-11-19).

Observations from the lab rotation (hands-on):
- Rotation discovery pattern: 60% of new items are infra misconfig, 30% code secrets, 10% dependency or supply-chain flags.
- Quick wins deployed during the lab: tightened staging network policies and added a pre-merge check (infra-lint) to flag missing ingress rules.

2) Secrets scanning and validation (owner: Sofia)
- Tools in play: TruffleHog (custom rules), internal scanner (scanner-v2), and Hashicorp Vault audit hooks.
- Recent noisy signal: ~120 alerts in the last 48h; after quick triage, ~85% were false positives (env var examples, long hashed strings, test fixtures).
- Decided immediate changes:
  - Update TruffleHog heuristics to ignore common fixture patterns (list kept in /confluence/SEC-Lab-Playbook).
  - Add a confidence score to scanner alerts (low/med/high) and push high-confidence only to oncall pager during off-hours.
  - Integrate scanner hits with Vault: if a secret identifier matches a Vault-managed credential, auto-create a high-priority ticket and rotate the secret.
- Outstanding risk: service account key rotation process is manual for a small set of older services.
  - Owner: Noah. Plan: schedule rotation automation spike (2d) and present in next sprint planning.

Notes-to-self / informal bits (common for Drive docs):
- "Sidenote: we keep getting flagged by GH token regex on fixtures — maybe fine-tune by token length + character class + surrounding context."
- "Question: do we want a weekly 'secrets-sweep' badge in console to surface average false-positive rate? Useful for product conversations."

3) Threat-modeling micro-workshop (owner: Ethan)
- Scope: Dedicated capacity control plane and customer routing policies (focus on compromise scenarios for multi-tenant config).
- Quick assumptions declared: dedicated pools are logically isolated but share control-plane orchestration components; rollout policy metadata is versioned in config-store.
- Threat hypotheses generated:
  A) Control-plane config-store compromise -> target: rollout metadata changed to route traffic to malicious endpoint.
     - Risk vector: compromised CI token or stolen deploy key.
     - Mitigations discussed: sign config-store snapshots (lightweight attestations), require MFA for config promotions, introduce a promotion audit webhook that streams diff to an internal watcher.
  B) KV cache poisoning of inference runtime -> target: malformed cached prompts cause hallucination leakage between tenants.
     - Risk vector: insufficient namespace isolation in cache keys.
     - Mitigations: prefix namespacing, TTL enforcement, sanitize serialized prompts before caching, add cache-read sandboxing test.
- Decision: prototype config snapshot signing and a diff-webhook (owner: Ethan, pairing with eng-platform). Prototype spike: deliverable by 2026-12-08.

4) Playbook updates and documentation (owner: Ava + Sofia)
- Update SEC-Lab-Playbook: add a new section "Rotation sprint: triage lab runbook" with checklists: pre-rotation environment sizing, scoped tickets for practice, post-run RCA template.
- Add sample queries for searching Vault logs for suspected rotations.

Action items (clear owners + dates):
- Jonah: RCA for JIRA-SEC-8421 (P0) — due 2026-11-22.
- Maya: add negative test for vendor SDK harness (JIRA-SEC-8430) — due 2026-11-19.
- Noah: automation spike to rotate legacy service account keys (2d spike, schedule by 2026-11-20).
- Ethan + Eng-Platform: prototype config snapshot signing & diff-webhook (spike PR target 2026-12-08).
- Sofia: update TruffleHog heuristics & add confidence score to scanner (2026-11-18).
- Ava: draft a new "rotation" section in SEC-Lab-Playbook and link examples (2026-11-21).

Follow-ups / questions for leadership:
- Budget ask: 2 engineer-weeks to automate service account rotation across legacy services (ask to Product/Infra).
- On-call policy: proposal to change high-confidence scanner hits to oncall paging outside business hours — needs SRE alignment.

Retrospective notes (what worked / what didn't):
- Worked: hands-on lab rotation catches configuration drift quickly; rotating the person running the lab exposes different heuristics.
- Didn't work: scanner noise is still high; needs engineering time to tune rules and reduce alert fatigue before rolling to oncall.

Appendix: short checklist for next rotation
- Host: Ava (2026-11-22)
- Environment: staging-3 snapshot, infra-lint enabled, TruffleHog update deployed to scanner-v2-dev
- Focus: secrets noise reduction + config promotion audit
- Expected artifacts: short RCA for any P0/P1 tickets discovered, updated playbook checklist PR.

Linked artifacts & refs: SEC-Lab-Playbook (Confluence), JIRA-SEC-8421, JIRA-SEC-8430, PR infra/pull/2891.
